{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793120556670,"sessionID":"ses_e81b142f3ffexRymGCb78h5TsD","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01DTmsqHw6c1Ed7trrffUoWh","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r5/nbody/nbody.cpp","content":"#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr double SOFTENING = 1e-9;\nconstexpr double DT = 0.01;\n\n// Number of target bodies processed together by the force kernel. Each target keeps its own\n// accumulation chain, so the summation order for every body is unchanged.\nconstexpr size_t kIBlock = 4;\n\nstruct Vec3 {\n    double x, y, z;\n    constexpr Vec3(const double x = 0, const double y = 0, const double z = 0) noexcept : x(x), y(y), z(z) {}\n};\n\nstruct Body {\n    Vec3 pos;\n    Vec3 vel;\n};\n\nvoid randomizeBodies(std::vector<Body>& bodies, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    for (auto& body : bodies) {\n        body.pos.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// Adds the contribution of body j to the force accumulated on body i.\ninline void accumulateForce(const Vec3& pj, const Vec3& pi, double& Fx, double& Fy, double& Fz) {\n    const double dx = pj.x - pi.x;\n    const double dy = pj.y - pi.y;\n    const double dz = pj.z - pi.z;\n    const double distSqr = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + SOFTENING;\n    const double invDist = 1.0 / std::sqrt(distSqr);\n    const double invDist3 = invDist * invDist * invDist;\n\n    Fx += dx * invDist3;\n    Fy += dy * invDist3;\n    Fz += dz * invDist3;\n}\n\n// Updates velocities of bodies [i0, i0 + B). Every body sums over j = 0..n-1 in increasing\n// order, exactly as the serial reference, so the results are bit-identical for any partitioning.\ntemplate <size_t B>\ninline void forceBlock(const Vec3* pos, Vec3* vel, size_t n, size_t i0) {\n    Vec3 pi[B];\n    double Fx[B] = {}, Fy[B] = {}, Fz[B] = {};\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < B; ++k) {\n        pi[k] = pos[i0 + k];\n    }\n\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        const Vec3 pj = pos[j];\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < B; ++k) {\n            accumulateForce(pj, pi[k], Fx[k], Fy[k], Fz[k]);\n        }\n    }\n\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < B; ++k) {\n        vel[i0 + k].x += DT * Fx[k];\n        vel[i0 + k].y += DT * Fy[k];\n        vel[i0 + k].z += DT * Fz[k];\n    }\n}\n\n// Computes forces on the locally owned bodies [begin, end) using the full position array.\nvoid computeForcesRange(const std::vector<Vec3>& pos, std::vector<Vec3>& vel, size_t begin, size_t end) {\n    const size_t n = pos.size();\n    const Vec3* p = pos.data();\n    Vec3* v = vel.data();\n\n    size_t i = begin;\n    for (; i + kIBlock <= end; i += kIBlock) {\n        forceBlock<kIBlock>(p, v, n, i);\n    }\n    for (; i < end; ++i) {\n        forceBlock<1>(p, v, n, i);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid integrateRange(std::vector<Vec3>& pos, const std::vector<Vec3>& vel, size_t begin, size_t end) {\n    for (size_t i = begin; i < end; ++i) {\n        pos[i].x += vel[i].x * DT;\n        pos[i].y += vel[i].y * DT;\n        pos[i].z += vel[i].z * DT;\n    }\n}\n\ndouble computeTotalEnergy(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    double energy = 0.0;\n    const size_t n = bodies.size();\n    \n    // Kinetic energy (assuming unit mass)\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        energy += 0.5 * (body.vel.x * body.vel.x + \n                        body.vel.y * body.vel.y + \n                        body.vel.z * body.vel.z);\n    }\n    \n    // Potential energy (assuming unit mass for all bodies)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            const double dx = bodies[j].pos.x - bodies[i].pos.x;\n            const double dy = bodies[j].pos.y - bodies[i].pos.y;\n            const double dz = bodies[j].pos.z - bodies[i].pos.z;\n            const double dist = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + SOFTENING);\n            energy -= 1.0 / dist;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return energy;\n}\n\n// Validate that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\nbool validateSimulation(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        // Check for NaN or Inf values\n        if (!std::isfinite(body.pos.x) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.y) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.z) ||\n            !std::isfinite(body.vel.x) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.y) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.z)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value in body state\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n        \n        // Check for extreme values (bodies shouldn't fly off to infinity)\n        const double maxPos = 1e6;\n        const double maxVel = 1e6;\n        if (std::abs(body.pos.x) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.y) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.z) > maxPos) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body position exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (std::abs(body.vel.x) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.y) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.z) > maxVel) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body velocity exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of bodies (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Number of simulation steps (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation (checks energy conservation)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\n// Runs the benchmark on all ranks. Returns the process exit code (identical on every rank).\nint runBenchmark(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    int numBodies = 1024;\n    int numSteps = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments (every rank parses identically)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numBodies = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numSteps = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (numBodies < 0) {\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            printf(\"Number of bodies must be non-negative\\n\");\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n        }\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"N-Body Simulation\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of bodies: %d\\n\", numBodies);\n        printf(\"Number of steps: %d\\n\", numSteps);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    const size_t n = static_cast<size_t>(numBodies);\n\n    // MPI datatype for Vec3 (three contiguous doubles)\n    MPI_Datatype vec3Type;\n    MPI_Type_contiguous(3, MPI_DOUBLE, &vec3Type);\n    MPI_Type_commit(&vec3Type);\n\n    // Block partition of bodies across ranks (remainder spread over the first ranks)\n    std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size);\n    {\n        const size_t base = n / static_cast<size_t>(size);\n        const size_t rem = n % static_cast<size_t>(size);\n        int offset = 0;\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            counts[r] = static_cast<int>(base + (static_cast<size_t>(r) < rem ? 1 : 0));\n            displs[r] = offset;\n            offset += counts[r];\n        }\n    }\n    const size_t lo = static_cast<size_t>(displs[rank]);\n    const size_t hi = lo + static_cast<size_t>(counts[rank]);\n\n    // Initialize bodies (deterministic, so every rank starts from the same state).\n    // Positions are kept fully replicated; velocities are only meaningful for owned bodies.\n    std::vector<Body> initial(n);\n    randomizeBodies(initial);\n    std::vector<Vec3> pos(n), vel(n);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        pos[i] = initial[i].pos;\n        vel[i] = initial[i].vel;\n    }\n    std::vector<Body>().swap(initial);\n\n    // Run simulation\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    const double start = MPI_Wtime();\n\n    for (int step = 0; step < numSteps; ++step) {\n        computeForcesRange(pos, vel, lo, hi);\n        integrateRange(pos, vel, lo, hi);\n        MPI_Allgatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, vec3Type, pos.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), vec3Type,\n                       MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    }\n\n    const double localElapsed = MPI_Wtime() - start;\n    double elapsed = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localElapsed, &elapsed, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Simulation time: %ld ms\\n\", static_cast<long>(elapsed * 1000.0));\n    }\n\n    int rc = 0;\n    const bool needFullState = printResults || validate;\n\n    if (needFullState) {\n        // Gather all velocities onto rank 0 (positions are already replicated everywhere)\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            MPI_Gatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, vec3Type, vel.data(), counts.data(), displs.data(), vec3Type, 0,\n                        MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        } else {\n            MPI_Gatherv(vel.data() + lo, counts[rank], vec3Type, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, vec3Type, 0,\n                        MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        }\n\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            std::vector<Body> bodies(n);\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n                bodies[i].pos = pos[i];\n                bodies[i].vel = vel[i];\n            }\n\n            // Print results for external validation\n            if (printResults) {\n                // Serialize body positions and velocities for hashing\n                std::vector<double> bodyData;\n                bodyData.reserve(n * 6);\n                for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n                    bodyData.push_back(body.pos.x);\n                    bodyData.push_back(body.pos.y);\n                    bodyData.push_back(body.pos.z);\n                    bodyData.push_back(body.vel.x);\n                    bodyData.push_back(body.vel.y);\n                    bodyData.push_back(body.vel.z);\n                }\n                print_results(bodyData, \"Bodies\");\n            }\n\n            // Validation: check that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\n            if (validate) {\n                printf(\"Validating simulation results...\\n\");\n\n                if (validateSimulation(bodies)) {\n                    // Report final energy for reference\n                    double finalEnergy = computeTotalEnergy(bodies);\n                    printf(\"Final energy: %.6f\\n\", finalEnergy);\n                    printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n                } else {\n                    printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n                    rc = 1;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    MPI_Bcast(&rc, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    MPI_Type_free(&vec3Type);\n    return rc;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n    const int rc = The tricky part is pinning this behavior in standard C++ since GCC's fp-contract=fast can silently re-fuse the operations across statements, and there's no clean per-statement way to forbid contraction without resorting to compiler-specific pragmas or ugly workarounds like volatile.\n\nSo my plan is to compile the whole target with -ffp-contract=off and then explicitly use std::fma only where the original inlined assembly actually shows FMA instructions (the distance-squared calculation and force update), while writing the velocity update and integration step as plain, non-fused expressions to match what the original compiled code actually does.\n\nFor the energy computation, contraction differences there are negligible since the result is only printed to six decimal places and isn't part of the hash — I'll accept that minor risk rather than matching FMA exactly there. I'll add the flag directly in CMake via target_compile_options to make the build deterministic.\n\nChecking the inlined assembly confirms the pattern holds across all N since compiled code doesn't vary by size: the force accumulation still uses fused multiply-add for distance-squared and force updates, the velocity update is plain multiply-then-add once contraction is off (matching the separate vmulpd/vaddpd instructions), and the position integration still uses a fused multiply-add matching the original instruction sequence.\n\nMy plan now is to revert the velocity update to its plain form, add the no-contraction flag to the CMake config, rebuild, and rerun tests against the inlined reference build rather than worrying about the non-inlined variant.\n\n","time":{"start":1793121888513,"end":1793121898677},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793122415169,"sessionID":"ses_e81b142f3ffexRymGCb78h5TsD","part":{"id":"prt_17e6c8e3f001jz6vzABdvzBO6f","messageID":"msg_17e6c82d70011i2bTUdhHmJop5","sessionID":"ses_e81b142f3ffexRymGCb78h5TsD","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing the kernel's scalar sqrt and divide operations are likely bottlenecked on divider throughput, so switching to 4-wide vectorized sqrt/div instructions could yield close to a 4x speedup depending on Zen3's actual throughput for these vector ops versus scalar.\n\nGiven this is worth pursuing for a 3-4x gain, I want to restructure the block kernel to help the SLP vectorizer recognize the 4-lane pattern — likely the issue is the AoS layout of position data causing gather-like loads instead of clean SIMD groups. Switching to SoA arrays for positions and forces per block should let the compiler vectorize the independent lanes properly.\n\nI'm also weighing whether GCC vector extensions can preserve the fused multiply-add needed for bit-exact distance computation, since GCC lacks a built-in elementwise fma like Clang does. I'll test an SoA-based forceBlock4 variant with scalar fma calls per lane to see if the compiler auto-vectorizes it back into proper SIMD fma instructions.\n\nActually, I suspect the real blocker is that std::sqrt defaults to setting errno on negative inputs, which forces GCC to emit a scalar sqrt with an error-check branch rather than a vectorized sqrt — that's likely why vsqrtpd isn't appearing, and the same constraint applies to the original code too.\n\nSince distSqr is always ≥ SOFTENING > 0 here, errno handling is irrelevant semantically, so adding `-fno-math-errno` as a build flag should be safe and would let the compiler vectorize sqrt.
